chapter: Retirement and the future of big bands
title: Bunny Briggs, dancer and singer with the band
summary: Barnet found Briggs dancing on a tabletop in Baltimore around 1941 and featured him until 1950, but his mother kept him from stardom.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: A guy that did work for me for a long period of time was Bunny Briggs.

One of the -- oh, the greatest dancer. We used to -- I had him on practically every Apollo show and other places. I had him where he couldn't even dance, he would just sing. We had numbers that he sang, and he had such a wonderful personality, I mean he broke up everyplace that we went into with Bunny. Bunny unfortunately had a big mother complex. He says, "Oh, my mother doesn't want me to be in show business. She'd rather I'd be running an elevator." And

he was completely dominated by her and I think he could have been a big star if it wasn't on account of this. Fortunately, I had the pleasure of having him with my band on many, many occasions. He was just an absolute blockbuster as far as breaking up a show.
Oh, he's a great dancer. I know I've heard him sing, too. But I didn't realize he'd worked with you. What year was it?
Oh, I found Bunny dancing on a tabletop in Baltimore back in, oh, about 1941, something like that. And he was with my band, oh, up till 1950.

Practically steadily. As steady as the band happened. I mean he was there. He was down in Birdland when it was known as The Clique. He was there with me. I had him with the '49 band. I had him in numerous -- every theater I ever played I made sure he was on the bill with me, including the Paramount and the -- in New York, and all of the other theaters around the country. I'm talking about the white theaters, too. I'm not only talking about the black theaters. And I also had him with the band, and occasionally where he couldn't dance, all he did was sing. And exhibited his personality. He's with Lionel Hampton now.
He does a lot of work with Lionel now.
I didn't know what he was doing now. I knew he worked with Duke briefly.
In the first Sacred Concert and some other dates.

Yeah. But he'd get away from home, he'd get homesick. He'd want to go home, you know. I said, "Buddy --," I had him out at Universal Pictures. They put him in one of these shorts as an audition. They were very interested. He says, "No, I've got to go home." I said, "Bunny, you don't know. You're on the verge of something here." "No, I've got to go home." It was really sad.
